en.title: Exodus Reveals Female Protagonist Voice Actor and New Trailer
en.summary: The upcoming Mass Effect-inspired RPG Exodus has finally shown off its female protagonist in a new trailer, revealing the voice actor behind the character. Players will have the choice between male and female versions of the lead, Jun Aslan.
en.body:
The highly anticipated spacefaring RPG **Exodus**, from developer **Archetype Entertainment**, has given players their first look and listen to the female version of its protagonist, Jun Aslan. This reveal comes via a brand-new story trailer, showcasing **Carina Conti** as the voice and performance capture artist for female Jun. Conti brings a wealth of acting experience to the role, having appeared in popular shows like **Good Trouble** and **Winning Time**, as well as the Sundance award-winning film **Junk**. Gamers might also recognize her from her leading role as Isabella Torrisi in **Mafia: The Old Country**.

Players have previously heard the male version of Jun, voiced by **Stephen Oyoung**, whose credits include blockbuster films such as **Mission: Impossible – The Final Reckoning** and video game roles like Mister Negative in **Marvel's Spider-Man 2** and Red Hood in **Gotham Knights**. **Archetype Entertainment** recently made adjustments to the male Jun's facial model based on community feedback, demonstrating a commitment to player input. Importantly, the developers have confirmed that regardless of the player's choice between male or female Jun, the core dialogue, overarching story, and romance options will remain consistent, though the performances will naturally differ.

## A Familiar Choice for RPG Fans

Allowing players to choose their protagonist's gender is a hallmark of many beloved RPGs, most notably the **Mass Effect** series, which **Exodus** clearly draws inspiration from. This approach allows for greater player immersion and personal connection to the narrative. The introduction of **Carina Conti** as the voice for female Jun adds another layer of polish to the game's presentation. While the male Jun's design was tweaked following player reactions, the focus now shifts to how the dual voice performances will shape the player's experience with Jun Aslan, a character described as a scrappy salvager turned space traveler.

## Meet Salt, the Awakened Sniper

Beyond the protagonist, **Exodus** also introduced another key character in its recent trailer: **Salt**. She is an 'Awakened,' a unique element in the game's universe described as hyper-intelligent animals capable of communicating with humans. **Salt** is slated to be a long-range sniper within the player's party, capable of deploying ink smokescreens for tactical advantage in combat. While **Salt** can be confrontational, her character is driven by a deep desire to protect others, adding emotional depth to the unfolding narrative. The game is being developed using the powerful **Unreal Engine 5**.

## What's Next

**Exodus** is slated for an April release, and with the protagonist's dual voice actors now revealed and key characters like **Salt** showcased, players can anticipate more story details and gameplay mechanics to be unveiled as the launch date approaches.

content_raw: We've seen the upcoming spacefaring sci-fi RPG Exodus from many angles already and even had an extensive hands-on preview where I got to play through an entire mission. Everything from its blend of shooter and RPG combat to the kinds of choices you'll make at pivotal moments as lead protagonist Jun Aslan. But two major things that've been kept under wraps until now were the character model and voice of female Jun – like Mass Effect, players can choose to play as a male or female version of the main character. Through a new story trailer, we finally saw and heard female Jun in action for the first time who is being voiced by actor Carina Conti. Conti has appeared in shows such as Good Trouble on Hulu and Winning Time on HBO, as well as the Sundance award-winning comedy-drama Junk (previously titled Little Death). She also had a leading role in Mafia: The Old Country as the character Isabella Torrisi, and now she'll be our scrappy salvager turned space traveler Jun Aslan in Exodus. Male Jun is being portrayed by actor Stephen Oyoung who has made appearances in movies such as Mission: Impossible – The Final Reckoning, The Wrecking Crew, and Twisters. And he has video game credits as Mister Negative in Marvel's Spider-Man and Spider-Man 2 and Red Hood in Gotham Knights. We've been able to hear his version of Jun throughout all previous content in Exodus, and more recently, developer Archetype Entertainment tweaked the face model of male Jun based on audience feedback. As previously stated in our preview and interview with Archetype, regardless of which version of Jun players choose, the dialogue, story, and romance options remain the same even if the performances will be different. In a conversation with both Conti and Oyoung, they jokingly mentioned that recording romance scenes were both traumatic and hilarious, but they also spoke to embodying Jun as a character. "I love her [female Jun], I'm a little bit obsessed with her! She embodies qualities that I really envision for my future self," Conti said. "Getting to practice those [qualities] within her over the course of six months was such a luxury. It was like, what if you already got to play this version of yourself where you are powerful, confident, and courageous, and a leader of men where you really have your ducks in a row." Exodus is set to launch on April 7, 2027 for PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X|S, and PC. Be sure to check out my last hands-on preview with Exodus covering the mission on the ship colony of Khonsu where we saved a species of intelligent frogs from control from an evil faction and made a game-changing decision about their fate. You can also read my interview with narrative director Drew Karphysyn (known for writing Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic and Mass Effect) where he explained choice and consequence in Exodus and how his time at BioWare shaped his upcoming work. Speaking of Mass Effect, I also interviewed Jennifer Hale and Mark Meer , the voices of Commander Shepar
